items.title: Building a great nation starts with happy families - PM
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: National development should not be measured solely by the grandeur of skyscrapers, technological advancements or an influx of investments, said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. Anwar said efforts to build a great nation must begin with the establishment of happy family institutions. Earlier, Anwar officiated the National Family Month 2026 celebration in Shah Alam, Selangor, today, which was also attended by his wife, Datuk Seri Dr Wan Azizah Wan Ismail, and Minister of Women, Family and Community Development Datuk Seri Nancy Shukri.

items.title: Myanmar plans April by-election, including in conflict areas
items.summary: Myanmar's military-appointed election commission has scheduled by-elections for April next year to fill dozens of parliamentary seats, state media said on Friday, including in areas impacted by a protracted civil war. The contest for vacant seats in 55 constituencies will be held on April 4, the Global New Light of Myanmar reported. The vote follows a general election held in December and January that was won overwhelmingly by the military-backed Union Solidarity and Development Party in the absence of any viable opposition.

items.title: Nine detained over teen's fatal stabbing in Sibu
items.summary: SIBU: Police have detained nine people, aged between 16 and 42, to assist a probe into the murder of a 19-year-old who is believed to have been stabbed during a fight at a public park in Jalan Gambir here early today. Sibu district police chief ACP Abang Zainal Abidin Abang Ahmad said all suspects were rounded up at several locations around Sibu between 10am and 4pm today following intelligence gathering and investigations by the Sibu police headquarters' Criminal Investigation Department (CID). Abang Zainal Abidin said the incident had also gone viral on social media.

items.title: Indonesian workers rally for Prabowo as women march against president
items.summary: JAKARTA: Hundreds of workers rallied in support of Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto on Saturday amid allegations that police illegally wiretapped him, while hundreds of women marched against the president's policies. Labour Party Chairperson Said Iqbal, leading the workers' rally, called for unity to support Prabowo and said he would mobilise union members against those who threaten the former general's presidency. Indonesian police have named four senior police officials as suspects accused of attempting to intercept Prabowo's communications, including a former police chief who is known as a loyalist of former president Joko Widodo.

items.title: Today's news in pictures - Saturday, Nov 7, 2026
items.summary: [[nid:1572964]] GEORGE TOWN – Hindu devotees make final preparations by shopping for festive essentials in Little India ahead of the Deepavali celebrations. NSTP/AURIS FAQRURAZZI [[nid:1572963]] GEORGE TOWN – Shoppers browse for festive goods in Little India as Hindu devotees carry out last-minute preparations for Deepavali. NSTP/HARI ANGGARA [[nid:1572961]] KUALA LUMPUR – The scene outside the residence of former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Tun Razak in Jalan Langgak Duta.

items.title: Melaka polls: MIC's sole candidate sacrifices family time to campaign for Gadek's future
items.summary: ALOR GAJAH: For Barisan Nasional candidate for Gadek S. Nadarajah, this Deepavali will be unlike previous celebrations as his campaign commitments leave little time for family gatherings. With the Melaka election campaign taking priority, even a planned lunch with his family remains uncertain as he continues making his rounds to meet voters. He said he had only managed to call his father this morning to check on the family's Deepavali preparations.

items.title: High-tide phenomenon may hit low-lying, coastal areas in Selangor tomorrow
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Residents in low-lying and coastal areas of Selangor have been urged to remain vigilant following the forecast of a high tide phenomenon, with water levels expected to reach up to 5.2 metres (m) tomorrow. Selangor Fire and Rescue Department operations assistant director, Ashrul Riezal Asbar, said the forecast was based on projections by the Department of Irrigation and Drainage (DID), with water levels in Klang recorded at 5.1 metres today. He said the situation could lead to water flows from the Sungai Buloh and Ijok areas to converge with the high tide, thereby increasing the risk of flooding in low-lying areas.

items.title: Fallen trees crush cars, damage shop in Kubang Semang and Prai
items.summary: SEBERANG PRAI: Two separate fallen tree incidents damaged two vehicles, a house and a shop in Kubang Semang and Prai today. Penang Fire and Rescue Department operations division assistant director John Sagun Francis said they were alerted to the incident in Prai at 6.01pm today. A team from the Prai fire station, supported by personnel from the Bandar Perda fire station, was dispatched to the scene at Desa Sutera Square along Jalan Sutera 3.

items.title: Flash floods hit Seberang Prai Tengah after torrential downpour
items.summary: BUKIT MERTAJAM: Several residential areas in Seberang Prai Tengah were inundated following a continuous downpour that lashed the district late this afternoon. The affected areas include Seberang Jaya, Permatang Rawa, Tanah Liat, Mengkuang Titi and Jalan Baharu. The Civil Defence Force (APM), which serves as the District Disaster Management Committee (JPBD) Secretariat, said response teams were deployed shortly after heavy rain began around 4.30pm.

items.title: Pressure on Israel must go beyond proposed resolutions, says Zahid
items.summary: ISTANBUL: The international community must take legal action against Israel to stop its military operations in Gaza, southern Lebanon and Syria. Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said pressure on Israel must go beyond proposed resolutions and translate into concrete action to ensure it respects and complies with previously agreed ceasefires. Zahid, who is also Umno president, said the party plans to collaborate with Seta on research through the Abdullah Badawi Research Institute to strengthen knowledge-sharing between Malaysia and Türkiye.

items.title: More than new clothes and sweets, Deepavali is about family and tradition
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, Nov 7 — Deepavali celebrations are not just about wearing new attire and preparing an array of traditional delicacies, but also about strengthening family bonds and preserving age-old traditions passed down through generations. For Singaporean P. Parvathy, 65, from Sengkang, a visit to Johor Bahru to shop for Deepavali essentials has become an annual tradition, while also giving her the opportunity to meet relatives living in the state. She said her visit to the Deepavali Bazaar at Jalan Ungku Puan here also allowed her to browse a variety of decorative items for the home, including floral ornaments to hang at the entrance, traditional attire and bangles.

items.title: Four injured in Seberang Jaya multi-vehicle pile-up
items.summary: SEBERANG JAYA: Four people were injured in a four-vehicle collision along Km134.8 of the North-South Expressway near Seberang Jaya this afternoon. "The accident involved four vehicles — two Perodua Myvi, a Toyota Alphard and a Honda Accord — with seven people involved in total," he said. Francis said that of the seven people, four sustained light injuries.

items.title: Delhi world's most polluted major city on eve of Diwali, Swiss group says
items.summary: * IQAir ranked Delhi first among the world's major cities at 10:35am (0505 GMT), with a US air quality index reading of 581, double that of Lahore in neighbouring Pakistan, at 285. * India's Central Pollution Control Board put Delhi's air quality index at 363 at 10 am, in the "very poor" category. * Friday's air quality in Delhi was the worst pre-Diwali air in eight years, local media said, citing official data.

items.title: Mara signs two LoCs with Turkish universities
items.summary: ISTANBUL: Majlis Amanah Rakyat (Mara) has strengthened Malaysia–Turkiye academic ties through collaborations with two Turkish universities, focusing on joint degree programmes, doctoral research and ship-design studies. The Letters of Collaboration (LoCs) were exchanged between Universiti Kuala Lumpur (UniKL) and Universiti Poly-Tech Malaysia (UPTM) with Sabancı University and Yildiz Technical University (YTU) here. Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi, Mara chairman Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki and newly-appointed Deputy Director-General (Education) Shahrizal Mohd Saderi witnessed the exchange.

items.title: This Deepavali, Anwar calls on Malaysians to celebrate differences and shared values
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 7 — The Deepavali celebration should serve as a platform to strengthen unity, bridge gaps between communities and foster values of compassion and concern for those in need. Deepavali Nalvaalthukkal ! (Deepavali greetings),” he added.

items.title: After deadly Paya Terubong landslide, Chow says DOSH must finish probe first
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Nov 7 — The Penang state government will decide whether to set up a State Commission of Inquiry (SCI) into the Taman Seri Rambai landslide in Paya Terubong once the state Department of Occupational Safety and Health (DOSH) completes its investigation and submits its findings and recommendations. Penang Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow said the state government would await the findings of the DOSH investigation before considering further action over the incident, which claimed the life of a 73-year-old doctor. “DOSH is conducting its investigation and will provide recommendations (to the state government) once it is completed.

items.title: Nothing to hide: Umno welcomes audit of Najib crowdfunding, says Asyraf
items.summary: ISTANBUL: Umno has nothing to hide and welcomes any audit of its RM50 million crowdfunding effort for former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak, said its secretary-general Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki. He said the party had been transparent from the start, with a separate account established for the Najib Razak Solidarity Fund following an Umno Supreme Council decision. Asyraf said the fund came from a crowdfunding effort and all the money came from the public.

items.title: Zahid says Malaysia stands ready to help Lebanon rebuild after conflict
items.summary: ISTANBUL, Nov 7 — Malaysia is ready to help Lebanon rebuild following the conflict that has affected the country, Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said. “Malaysia and Lebanon share a special friendship, particularly through Malaysia’s involvement in peacekeeping operations under the Malaysian Battalion (MALBATT) since 2007. Insya-Allah,” he said.

items.title: Najib’s lawyers seek immediate transfer home, say King’s decree must be executed today
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 7 — Lawyers for Datuk Seri Najib Razak are contesting the Attorney General’s Chambers’ (AGC) decision to temporarily suspend his house arrest, demanding the former prime minister be transferred to his home immediately. In a media statement today, the legal firm Messrs Shafee & Co. argued that the AGC’s “temporary suspension” of the house arrest order contradicts the King’s explicit decree issued this morning. The statement noted that the AGC issued a subsequent media statement 57 minutes after the King’s decree, which did not reference the royal order.

items.title: Anwar extends Deepavali greetings, calls for stronger national unity
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Deepavali celebration should serve as a platform to strengthen unity, bridge gaps between communities and foster values of compassion and concern for those in need. Deepavali Nalvaalthukkal ! (Deepavali greetings)," he added.

items.title: Asyraf: No need for A-G to meet King over Najib's house arrest
items.summary: ISTANBUL: There is no need for the Attorney-General to be told to meet Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, to explain legal issues surrounding Datuk Seri Najib Razak's house arrest, says an Umno leader. The party's secretary-general Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki said the King's power to grant pardons was clearly enshrined in the Federal Constitution. The Prime Minister's Office said Dusuki would also explain legal questions arising from the High Court's discharge order following payment of the RM50 million fine, a condition for the house arrest.

items.title: Penang sets aside RM4.5m to grow startups, AI adoption and digital economy
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Nov 7 — The Penang government has allocated RM4.5 million in its 2027 budget to support technology startups, accelerate digitalisation among small and medium enterprises (SMEs) and expand the use of artificial intelligence (AI) across the state’s economy. “In (the state’s) Budget 2027, the state government has set aside RM4.5 million for Digital Penang; it will support technology start-ups, help small and medium enterprises go digital, and use AI across our economy. Also present at the AI Future Makers Bootcamp 2026 were chairman Lukas J.Tan and SEGi College Penang head of student experience Vincent Tung Chin Aun.

items.title: King's decree already answered A-GC's questions, says Najib's lawyers
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The decree by His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia on Datuk Seri Najib Razak's conditional pardon had already addressed all questions raised by the Attorney-General's Chambers (AGC), his lawyers said. In a statement, Messrs Shafee & Co, representing the former prime minister, said the decree issued through Istana Negara today had made clear that the Conditional Pardon Order dated Sept 18 was issued by the Yang di-Pertuan Agong under Article 42 of the Federal Constitution. Shafee & Co said the A-GC could not rely on the High Court's Order of Discharge on Payment of Fine, issued on Friday following Najib's payment of the RM50 million fine, to alter the terms of the royal decree.

items.title: Melaka polls: Ab Rauf's track record offers confidence in BN-PN manifesto delivery
items.summary: MELAKA: The Barisan Nasional-Perikatan Nasional (BN-PN) joint manifesto provides a comprehensive roadmap for Melaka's development, with a focus on economic opportunities and public welfare, say political analysts. They said the 113 initiatives outlined in the manifesto addressed key concerns affecting the people, including the cost of living, affordable housing, employment opportunities and economic growth. Political analyst Dr Mohammad Tawfik Yaakub said the proposals, which include free water, affordable housing, employment opportunities and a RM30 billion investment target, reflected an effort to address the needs of different segments of society.

items.title: Nancy wants 42,000 men to seek health support and join family decisions
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Nov 7 — The Ministry of Women, Family and Community Development (KPWKM) is targeting 42,000 men to benefit from government-provided well-being services for men, as part of efforts to raise awareness of the importance of healthcare among them. Women, Family and Community Development Minister Datuk Seri Nancy Shukri said the initiative also encouraged men to seek relevant health information and services with their partners, particularly when making decisions about family health. She was speaking at the November National Family Month 2026 celebration, which was launched by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and attended by his wife, Bandar Tun Razak MP Datuk Seri Dr Wan Azizah Wan Ismail, Deputy Women, Family and Community Development Minister Lim Hui Ying, and Selangor State Executive Councillor for Women and Community Welfare Anfaal Saari.

items.title: BN-PN must ensure vote transfer to secure Melaka victory, says KJ
items.summary: Former Umno Youth chief Khairy Jamaluddin said the arrangement would translate into electoral success only if grassroots supporters were prepared to back candidates from allied parties, even when their preferred party was not contesting. He said the Melaka election would serve as an important test of whether the cooperation could deliver another electoral victory, following the formula adopted in the recent Negri Sembilan election. Khairy said the arrangement required Pas and PN supporters to back BN candidates in constituencies where their parties were not contesting, and vice versa.

items.title: Najib's lawyers want ex-PM transferred to Langgak Duta tonight
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Datuk Seri Najib Razak's lawyers have called on the Commissioner-General of Prisons to transfer the former prime minister to his Jalan Langgak Duta residence tonight, in line with the King's decree. Messrs Shafee & Co also urged the Attorney-General's Chambers to immediately withdraw the "temporary deferment" of Najib's house arrest. "His Majesty's order must be implemented today," the firm said in a statement.

items.title: Zahid: There should be no "delaying tactics" in implementing Najib's house arrest
items.summary: ISTANBUL: Umno president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said there should be no "delaying tactics" to stall the implementation of Datuk Seri Najib Razak's house arrest following the payment of the RM50 million fine. Zahid said the matter must be complied with by all parties, including the Attorney-General's Chambers (A-GC). The initial RM210 million fine was also reduced to RM50 million.

items.title: All eyes on Nov 14 as police strengthen readiness for Melaka vote
items.summary: MELAKA, Nov 7 — The Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) is strengthening its level of preparedness to ensure public safety and order are maintained throughout the 16th Melaka State Election, which will be held on Nov 14. According to a post on the Melaka Police Facebook page, Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail, in his address during a working visit to the Melaka Contingent Police Headquarters (IPK) yesterday, touched on several matters, including duty assignment, security management and the responsibilities of every personnel in ensuring the smooth conduct of the election process. According to the post, Mohd Khalid also reminded PDRM personnel to safeguard the confidentiality of official information, strengthen esprit de corps and ensure compliance with the chain of command and control to guarantee the effectiveness of every assignment.

items.title: King's prerogative to pardon Najib cannot be questioned, says Anwar
items.summary: SHAH ALAM: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the prerogative of His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, to grant a conditional pardon to former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak could not be questioned. He said the decision on Najib's pardon in the SRC International Sdn Bhd case was based on the King's decree, with all preparations for its implementation already carried out. Earlier today, Istana Negara said the conditional pardon granted to Najib on Sept 18 was clear, explicit and unambiguous, and unrelated to any other cases involving him.

items.title: Saifuddin Nasution wants schools, police and health authorities to share data on at-risk students
items.summary: KULIM, Nov 7 — The Ministry of Home Affairs (KDN), the Ministry of Education (MOE), and the Ministry of Health (MOH) must strengthen their cooperation and information-sharing to address various security issues and create a safe school ecosystem. Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said these three ministries cannot work in isolation when dealing with the various issues that arise within schools. Saifuddin Nasution emphasised that collaboration among the three ministries is crucial, given that the school security ecosystem encompasses approximately 5.2 million students across 12,000 schools nationwide, a situation that necessitates information-sharing and integrated action among the relevant agencies.

items.title: Two step-sisters killed after car skids and crashes on PLUS highway near Tanjong Malim
items.summary: IPOH, Nov 7 — Two step-siblings died when the vehicle they were in skidded in an accident at Kilometre 388 of the North-South Expressway (Plus) southbound, near Tanjong Malim today. Muallim district police chief Supt Khalid Mohamad said an 18-year-old girl was pronounced dead at the scene, while a six-year-old girl who suffered severe injuries died while receiving treatment at the Slim River Hospital. Earlier, Perak Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) assistant director (Operations) Sabarodzi Nor Ahmad said a team from the Tanjong Malim Fire and Rescue Station was dispatched to the scene after receiving a call regarding the accident at 8.35am.

items.title: A-G seeking audience with Sultan Ibrahim to explain Najib house arrest issue
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Attorney-General has sought an audience with His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, to express his position on complying with the royal decree on the Conditional Pardon Order granted to former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak. The Prime Minister's Office, in a statement, said the A-G, Tan Sri Mohd Dusuki Mokhtar, will also explain the legal questions arising from the High Court's Release Order following the payment of the RM50 million fine, which was a precondition for Najib's house arrest. Najib was convicted of misappropriating RM42 million in SRC International funds and began serving his 12-year prison sentence at Kajang Prison on Aug 23, 2022.

items.title: Fahmi says online banking remains safe despite cyberattacks and Bank Rakyat hack
items.summary: DOHA, Nov 7 — The country’s online banking system and financial transactions remain secure despite attempted cyberattacks by non-state actors, including a recent hacking incident involving Bank Rakyat’s website, Communications Minister and Madani government spokesperson Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said. He said the hacking attempts detected so far had not resulted in data theft or affected the country’s online banking operations. On the hacking incident involving Bank Rakyat’s website, Fahmi said it was confined to changes to the website’s appearance and involved a third-party-managed site.

items.title: A-G should take leave over Najib house arrest issue, says KJ
items.summary: ALOR GAJAH: Attorney-General Tan Sri Mohd Dusuki Mokhtar should take immediate leave pending police investigations into reports lodged against him over the issue surrounding Datuk Seri Najib Razak's conditional pardon, Khairy Jamaluddin said. "When police reports are lodged, investigations must be carried out. Khairy said several police reports had been lodged against Dusuki, including by Umno Youth .

items.title: Respect King's powers to grant pardons, says Wee Ka Siong
items.summary: Wee said this in calling for the King's powers to grant pardons to be respected. He said there should be no contradictions of the decisions made by His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, concerning former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak's house arrest. The Attorney-General's Chambers said today that seeking a court ruling on Najib's house arrest did not override the King's power to grant pardons.

items.title: Zahid receives courtesy call from Malaysian Honorary Consul in Bursa
items.summary: ISTANBUL: Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi today received a courtesy call from Malaysia's Honorary Consul in Bursa, Turkiye, Datuk Cevdet Sefer. The 30-minute meeting began at 11am (4pm Malaysian time) at Zahid's hotel here. Zahid also discussed the development of the Malaysian Institute of Marine Engineering Technology in Lumut, Perak.

items.title: Mak Yong, Wayang Kulit master Che Mat named Living National Heritage
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: Nearly six decades of dedication to preserving Kelantan's Mak Yong and Wayang Kulit traditions have earned Che Mat Jusoh, an Adiguru (master practitioner) of traditional performing arts at Universiti Sains Malaysia (USM), recognition as a Living National Heritage (WAKOH) figure for 2026. In a statement today, USM said the prestigious honour was conferred by the National Heritage Department under the Tourism, Arts and Culture Ministry in appreciation of his longstanding efforts to safeguard the traditional art forms, which are an integral part of the nation's cultural heritage. The university said the recognition was conferred during the 6th National Heritage Declaration Ceremony, held recently at the ministry, where 39 heritage elements were also officially declared National Heritage.

items.title: Flood evacuees in Selangor, Perak nearly triple to over 4,000 in hours
items.summary: In SELANGOR , the number of flood evacuees still sheltering at PPS this afternoon rose to 3,798 from 128 families at two centres, compared with 1,206 from 316 families at nine centres this morning. According to the Social Welfare Department’s (JKM) InfoBencana portal, PPS Sekolah Agama Batu Lapan Ijok is sheltering 2,999 evacuees from 67 families, while 799 evacuees from 61 families are at Sekolah Kebangsaan (SK) Parit Mahang. Meanwhile, in PERAK , the number of flood and storm evacuees rose to 270 from 79 families this afternoon, compared with 198 from 58 families this morning, across the Hilir Perak and Manjung districts.

items.title: AG seeks audience with King to clarify Najib’s house arrest issue, says Anwar
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Nov 7 — Attorney General Tan Sri Mohd Dusuki Mokhtar has requested an audience with His Majesty, Sultan Ibrahim, to discuss former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak’s house arrest in his SRC International case, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said today. “I have asked for the Attorney General to immediately meet the Agong to ‘ mohon ampun ’ (apologise) and explain why that decision was accepted for the SRC case, but there is a problem as it involves the second case, which is the 1MDB case. Earlier, Anwar said he wanted to avoid this house arrest matter from becoming politicised.

items.title: Zahid, Lebanese deputy PM discuss post-conflict reconstruction
items.summary: ISTANBUL: Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi yesterday received courtesy calls from his Lebanese counterpart Dr Tarek Mitri and the Developing Eight (D-8) Organisation for Economic Cooperation secretary-general Sohail Mahmood. Zahid said his discussion with Mitri focused on security developments in Lebanon and post-conflict recovery efforts to help its people rebuild their lives. Zahid said Malaysia and Lebanon share close, friendly ties, particularly through the deployment of the Malaysian Battalion (Malbatt) under the United Nations Interim Force in Lebanon since 2007.

items.title: PM congratulates Kedah's top STA 2026 school SMA Nahdhah Hasanah
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has congratulated Sekolah Menengah Agama Nahdhah Hasanah in Melele, Kodiang, after it emerged as the top-performing school in Kedah in the 2026 Sijil Tinggi Agama (STA) examination. In a post on X today, Anwar said the school's achievement was undoubtedly underpinned by the exceptional dedication of its teachers and the sacrifices of parents. "I share in the joy of the great achievement of the students of SMA Nahdhah Hasanah.

items.title: Bukit Aman suspects cocaine-in-shoes arrest at Hong Kong airport linked to Malaysia drug bust
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 7 — The arrest of a Hong Kong man with about one kilogramme of cocaine concealed in his shoes at Hong Kong International Airport after arriving from Kuala Lumpur last Wednesday is believed to be linked to an international drug trafficking syndicate recently crippled by the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM). “We believe the syndicate has been crippled following the arrest of a Hong Kong national believed to be the syndicate leader and a local recruiter, as announced at yesterday’s press conference,” he said when contacted today. Media reports today said a 36-year-old Hong Kong man was arrested last Wednesday after customs officers found cocaine estimated to be worth HK$600,000 (RM311,000) during an inspection at Hong Kong International Airport following his arrival from Malaysia.

items.title: Zahid, Erdoğan discuss lifting Malaysia–Turkiye trade to US$10 billion by 2030
items.summary: ISTANBUL: Malaysia–Turkiye strategic ties must go beyond traditional cooperation and translate into concrete initiatives, Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said. Zahid said this after a 30-minute meeting with Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan on the sidelines of the 2026 TRT World Forum here yesterday. "It also speeds up the implementation of Malaysia–Turkiye strategic cooperation, in line with the countries' Comprehensive Strategic Partnership," he said in a statement.

items.title: Tourism Ministry open to helping international event organisers facing funding challenges, says Tiong
items.summary: SIBU, Nov 7 — The Ministry of Tourism, Arts and Culture (Motac) is prepared to consider collaborating with and providing assistance to organisers of international events in Malaysia, particularly those facing financial constraints. Minister Datuk Seri Tiong King Sing said the move was aimed at encouraging more international events to be held in the country while attracting greater participation from overseas. Tiong said the ministry would also explore possible forms of collaboration and assistance to help organisers address their financial challenges.

items.title: DAP yet to discuss replacing Anthony Loke as transport minister, says party vice-chairman
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 7 — DAP has yet to discuss a replacement for Transport Minister Anthony Loke, whose resignation remains conditional on former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak returning home to serve the remainder of his prison sentence under house arrest. DAP vice-chairman Syahredzan Johan said discussions about a potential successor would be premature because Loke’s resignation had not taken effect, the New Straits Times reported. Loke, who is also DAP secretary-general, reaffirmed yesterday that his resignation would take effect only when Najib physically returned home to begin serving his sentence under house arrest.

items.title: Teenager, 19, dies after being stabbed during alleged argument at Sibu park
items.summary: SIBU, Nov 7 — A 19-year-old youth died after being stabbed in the chest during an incident at a public park along Jalan Gambir here around midnight last night. It is understood that nearby residents heard a woman screaming from the direction of the park, prompting them to alert the police. When contacted today, Sibu District Police Chief ACP Abang Zainal Abidin Abang Ahmad confirmed that the case was still under investigation.

items.title: Security presence disappears from Najib’s Taman Duta residence as house arrest remains on hold
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 7 — The security presence outside former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak’s residence was nowhere to be seen today, a day after the Taman Duta property was placed under tight security ahead of his anticipated return under house arrest. The heightened security came as preparations were made for Najib’s expected return after he paid a RM50 million fine in the SRC International corruption case, fulfilling a key condition of a royal pardon allowing him to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest until August 23, 2028. Despite the absence of security personnel today, local and international journalists remained stationed near the residence, awaiting further developments.

items.title: Integrity must go hand in hand with academic success, Perlis Raja Muda tells UniSIRAJ graduates
items.summary: Raja Muda of Perlis Tuanku Syed Faizuddin Putra Jamalullail, who is also UniSIRAJ Chancellor, said knowledge developed one’s ability to think and solve problems, while good manners reflected one’s values. “Ensure that academic excellence and expertise are always accompanied by strong moral values and principles,” he said at the 9th UniSIRAJ Convocation Ceremony at Dewan 2020 here today. Tuanku Syed Faizuddin Putra said that in an era of artificial intelligence (AI) and digital advancement, the pursuit of knowledge must always go hand in hand with noble values and strong principles.

items.title: The journey home begins: Deepavali rush brings slow traffic to major highways across Malaysia
items.summary: “Traffic was also slow at the Johor Causeway, from Woodlands Checkpoint (CIQ) in Singapore to Sultan Iskandar CIQ in Johor in the northbound direction, while congestion was reported on the Second Link Expressway, from the Second Link Bridge to Sultan Abu Bakar CIQ in Johor, also northbound,” they said when contacted today. Traffic volume had also increased on the North-South Expressway Central Link (ELITE), affecting the northbound stretches from Gamuda Cove to Bandar Saujana Putra and Putra Heights to Shah Alam, as well as the southbound stretch from Putra Heights to Gamuda Cove. Meanwhile, on the Sungai Besi Expressway (BESRAYA), traffic was slow on the northbound stretches from Bandar Tasik Selatan to Kuchai and Serdang to Pekan Sungai Besi.

items.title: Umno leaders lodge police reports, Dr Akmal demands action on Najib’s house arrest delay
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 7 — Several Umno leaders in Johor have lodged a police report over the delay in implementing former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak’s house arrest, as Umno Youth chief Datuk Dr Muhammad Akmal Saleh called for similar reports to be filed nationwide. Pontian Umno chief Datuk Seri Ahmad Maslan, who is also a party supreme council member, lodged the report at the Benut police station at 12.30pm today, accompanied by his deputy Mohd Sumali Reduan, division vice-chief Jamaludin Abd Majid and several grassroots leaders. “A police report was lodged over the delay in implementing the house arrest order for Najib, which should have been carried out,” Ahmad said in a Facebook post.

items.title: GrabCar’s auto-accept booking system breaches gig workers’ rights, tribunal rules
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Nov 7 — The Gig Workers Tribunal (TPG) has ruled on three disputes involving e-hailing drivers and GrabCar Sdn Bhd, including awarding RM2,000 in compensation to one driver while upholding the deactivation of another driver’s account over misconduct involving passengers. According to Kesuma, the tribunal partially upheld an e-hailing driver’s financial claim against GrabCar in the first case, involving earnings from Saver bookings and the ‘Cashback and Advance Booking’ incentive. “The tribunal also found that GrabCar’s use of the ‘Auto Accept’ and ‘Fast Cancel’ mechanisms on its digital platform violated Section 8(1)(b) and (c) of the Gig Workers Act 2025 (Act 872),” the ministry said, noting that the provisions safeguard gig workers’ right to know the type of service and the agreed payment before accepting a job.

items.title: Bank Rakyat blames third-party glitch for website outage, says customer funds and data safe
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 7 — Bank Rakyat said today that a disruption to its corporate website was caused by a technical problem involving a third-party service provider, assuring customers that their deposits, personal information and banking services remained unaffected. In a statement posted on Facebook, the bank said the disruption was confined to its corporate website, while its banking systems and operations continued to function normally. “Customers can continue to carry out their banking transactions as usual through alternative channels, including the iRakyat website, iRakyat mobile application, BRICK, QR2E and i-bizRAKYAT,” the bank said.

items.title: Penang pledges land titles for all 28 Tamil schools, with five secured so far
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Nov 7 — The Penang State Government is committed to ensuring that all 28 Sekolah Jenis Kebangsaan Tamil (SJKT) in the state secure their respective land titles, as part of efforts to strengthen educational facilities. Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow said as of June, land titles had been successfully secured for five schools, with plans to secure titles for another five within the next two to three years. “In its efforts to strengthen educational facilities, the state government is also committed to ensuring that all 28 SJKT in Penang secure their respective land titles.

items.title: Jalaluddin denies plot to oust Negeri Sembilan MB, says no-confidence vote never discussed
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Nov 7 — Negeri Sembilan Umno chief Datuk Seri Jalaluddin Alias has denied plotting to oust Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim, dismissing speculation that a vote of no confidence was being planned amid uncertainty over the state’s political leadership. Jalaluddin said no such move had been discussed at a meeting of the state Umno leadership today, insisting that claims of rival factions within the party were unfounded. According to Utusan Malaysia , Jalaluddin was speaking after a Negeri Sembilan Umno liaison committee meeting at Wisma Umno in Seremban today.

items.title: ECRL Phase 1 completed, on track for Dec 12 launch
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 7 — The East Coast Rail Link (ECRL) has reached a major milestone with the completion and handover of Phase 1 from Kota Bharu, Kelantan, to Gombak, Selangor, to the project owner, Malaysia Rail Link Sdn Bhd (MRL). MRL, in a statement today, said China Communications Construction (ECRL) Sdn Bhd (CCCECRL), the Engineering, Procurement, Construction and Commissioning (EPCC) contractor for the project, officially handed over the 523-kilometre (km) Kota Bharu-Gombak alignment today, marking that the railway system is fully ready for commercial operations, scheduled to commence on Dec 12. It said the handover coincides with the commencement of the ECRL Trial Operations Programme today, which will run until Dec 2 as the final phase of preparations ahead of the launch of passenger services.

items.title: Mardi to tighten safety procedures across Malaysia after worker dies from bee stings, says D-G
items.summary: Mardi director-general Dr Sanimah Simoh said the measures would be implemented at all Mardi research stations nationwide to ensure that occupational safety and health remained a priority and to minimise the risk of accidents. She said the matter had been discussed at the Mardi senior management meeting, with several follow-up measures planned to strengthen compliance with existing safety SOPs. “Mardi management takes staff safety seriously, especially for those working in the field.

items.title: Fomca’s 72-hour food stockpiling advice not a government directive, says Mat Sabu
items.summary: MELAKA, Nov 7 — The government has not issued any directive for the public to stock up on food supplies for a 72-hour period as recommended by the Federation of Malaysian Consumer Associations (Fomca). Agriculture and Food Security Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Sabu advised consumers not to panic buy, but instead to continue shopping according to their daily needs as usual. In another development, he said the government aims to implement 5,000 Agro Madani Sales programmes nationwide, compared to the 3,400 programmes that have been held so far.

items.title: Sarawak polls: Fadillah dismisses candidacy speculation, says GPS machinery ready (VIDEO)
items.summary: KUCHING, Nov 7 — Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Amar Fadillah Yusof has brushed off speculation that he may contest in the 13th Sarawak state election. He was also asked about the key dates announced by the Election Commission (EC) for the state election. Fadillah, who is Parti Pesaka Bumiputera Bersatu (PBB) senior vice president and Gabungan Parti Sarawak (GPS) parliamentary chief whip, said PBB and GPS election machinery was already prepared, with preparations having been carried out since the previous state election.

items.title: Kelantan tops list of 3,045 flood hotspots as ministry prepares for monsoon
items.summary: The ministry said the DID National Flood Forecasting and Warning Centre (PRABN) issued 103 bulletins, comprising 64 early flood forecast bulletins and 39 flood warning bulletins, during the 2025/2026 North-east Monsoon season from November 13, 2025, to March 31, 2026. “A total of 799 flood incidents were recorded nationwide, comprising 480 monsoon floods, 274 flash floods, 25 cases of stagnant flooding and 20 coastal floods,” it said. The ministry said 614 flood warning sirens and 197 surveillance cameras were also in place at strategic locations nationwide to support flood monitoring and early warning efforts.
